candidates: In Storybook story files, every key in the meta `args` object must exactly match an actual prop name on the component under test; a mismatched key (e.g., a typo or a stale name) is silently ignored and the corresponding control will have no effect on the component.

In Storybook story files, story render functions must accept and spread `args` (e.g., `(args: ComponentProps) => <Component {...args} />`) so that controls wired through meta `args` actually reach the component at runtime; static render functions that hardcode all props will not reflect any control or global changes.

Do not initialize a prop-derived value with `useState` when the value must stay in sync with the prop over time; `useState(prop)` only captures the value at mount and ignores subsequent prop changes. Compute the value inline or with `useMemo` so it always reflects the latest prop.

All async operations that can reject (e.g., clipboard writes, dynamic imports, fetch calls) must have explicit error handling via a `.catch()` handler or a `try/catch` block to prevent silent, unhandled promise rejections.
Use `logger` from `storybook/internal/client-logger` for all client-side (browser) logging in this codebase instead of `console.log`, `console.error`, or other `console` methods.

When a styled component's visual appearance is driven by a prop (e.g., `isExpanded`, `withSource`), verify that the prop is explicitly forwarded with the current state or derived value at every render callsite; omitting it means the styled component will not respond to state changes.

In this project, `Button` and `ToggleButton` components whose visible text children already provide a clear accessible name must explicitly set `ariaLabel={false}`; this signals intentional reliance on children for the accessible name rather than an accidental omission of an aria-label.

In TypeScript interface declarations, each property and its preceding JSDoc comment must appear on its own line; never merge multiple property declarations or a property and its JSDoc comment onto a single line.
